longForm.verdict: Planning Center is a modular suite that a church can explore without immediately paying for every product. The decision is not whether the free tier is attractive; it is whether the eventual mix of products, limits and US-oriented finance assumptions will form a coherent UK operating system.

decisionLens.heading: Free entry reduces procurement risk, not implementation work.
decisionLens.text: A church can begin with People and capacity-limited free product tiers, but a connected suite still requires decisions about ownership, permissions, hand-offs and the paid thresholds that arrive as adoption grows.

sections.heading: Starting with the product that solves the immediate job
sections.question: Can the church learn before committing to a whole suite?
paragraphs: Planning Center documents People as free and offers capacity-limited free tiers across its product range. Its product set covers people records, services, groups, registrations, giving and check-in.

That makes a small, focused start possible. Choose one operational problem, such as service planning or people records, then set a review point before adding more products and creating a harder-to-manage stack.

sections.heading: The cost is distributed across products
sections.question: What happens when several teams reach paid limits at once?
paragraphs: Planning Center’s published model varies by product and usage. A free tier is therefore useful for evaluation, but it is not a reliable proxy for the long-term cost of a multi-team church.

Build a one-year cost model for the specific products, records, registrations and donation workflows the church expects to use. Include currency, payment availability and any tools that remain outside the suite.

sections.heading: UK finance and data questions
sections.question: Which assumptions still need direct confirmation?
paragraphs: The current profile confirms free-tier information and broad product capability. It does not confirm UK Gift Aid support, payment availability, UK-specific contractual terms or a complete data-processing position.

Planning Center publishes information-security material and user data-export guidance, which are valuable starting points. A UK church should still ask the supplier to demonstrate the exact exporting, permissions, payment and data-protection arrangements it needs.

userFeedback.summary: This profile does not use an independent review score or a collected user-review sample. Its assessment is based on Planning Center’s free-tier, security and data-management documentation.
themes: Independent user-feedback coverage has not yet been researched for this profile.
A staged trial is most useful when it tests the hand-offs between the products a church expects to adopt.
userFeedback.caveat: No conclusion about user satisfaction should be drawn from this research gap.

faq.question: Can a church use Planning Center for free?
faq.answer: Planning Center documents People as free and publishes capacity-limited free tiers for its other products. Paid costs vary by product and usage, so plan for the product mix a church expects to keep.

faq.question: Does Planning Center support UK Gift Aid?
faq.answer: Not confirmed in this profile. Verify the current UK payment, Gift Aid and finance workflow directly with the supplier before relying on its Giving product.

faq.question: Can Planning Center data be exported?
faq.answer: Planning Center publishes data-export guidance for People. Confirm the specific records, formats and access controls the church needs before relying on an exit or migration plan.

externalReviews.note: This is a profile for Planning Center Services, not an aggregate review of the whole Planning Center suite.
